re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +64
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T06:51:31Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +64
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T06:51:31Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1597._

> ℹ️ **2 resolved thread(s) excluded.**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 3

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The scenario fix is evidence-driven but misses the line that actually matters for E1: the pre-flight compaction trigger (`shouldCompact` = window − window~/4 = **12288**), not the 16384 guard line. The PR's own measured E1 basis (12898) sits ~600 tokens past that trigger, and I reproduced the failure: the changed test runs red on this linux CI-class runner at the E1 `hi!` wait (`header_badge_pty_test.dart:98`, 90s TimeoutException, status row `ctx 80% (13.0k/16.4k)` + `Compacting context…` mid-E1) — the same mid-compaction face as the Oct-14 nightly red.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — E1 deterministically enters the compaction chain (12.9k floor > 12288 trigger, floor can't drop under it); the nightly on this branch will stay red. Fix: shrink per-read size / grow count so the E1 floor clears 12288 with margin (details + repro in the inline thread).
- 💡 SUGGESTION — pin the scenario shape to `hideProtectTailEntries` / trigger arithmetic with a static guard so constant drift fails the gate, not the nightly.

**Next Steps**:
1. Re-derive the lean-read shape against `CompactionSettings.forWindow(window)` (e.g. ~30 × 60-line reads: turn-1 ≈ 18.5k > 16384, E1 floor ≈ 10.4k < 12288), re-measure, and run the PTY leg on a linux hosted runner (openpty works there) before re-submitting.
2. `dart analyze` is clean and the turn-1 fold/badge legs pass locally — that part of the scenario is sound; keep it.
3. After a genuinely green nightly, remove the file from `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (still listed since 2026-10-10) per the wire_serve_cli precedent (#1484).

---

### Thread 4

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {"head":"7247c3e01482f4f592be3e9fe0632e519322bb54","verdict":"REQUEST_CHANGES","blocking":1,"important":0,"suggestions":1,"at":"2026-10-14T05:28:39.248Z","source":"pr_review.json"} -->
🤖 Automated review record. Please do not edit or reply.

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

🚨 **BLOCKING: E1 still rides a compaction edge — the scenario was moved off the 16384 guard line but onto the 12288 `shouldCompact` trigger; reproduced red on a CI-class runner**

The fix compares the measured E1 request basis (12.9k) against the **over-window guard line (16384)** — but the pre-flight auto-compactor fires on a **different, lower line**: `shouldCompact` triggers when `contextTokens > contextWindow − reserveTokens` (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart:488`), and `CompactionSettings.forWindow(16384)` sets `reserveTokens = 16384 ~/ 4 = 4096` (`compaction.dart:452-457`) → **trigger = 12288 tokens**. The PR's own measurement puts E1 at **12898 — ~600 tokens PAST the trigger**, not 3.4k short of safety:

- `16384 − 4096 = 12288` (pre-flight compaction fires above this)
- measured E1 basis `12898 > 12288` → E1 enters the compaction chain **every run**, deterministically
- the post-fold floor can't get back under the trigger: it is the protected 8-record tail (8 × ~923 tok ≈ 7.4k) + ~5.5k fixed overhead (system prompt + E1 turn + summary + receipt records) ≈ 12.9k regardless of how many lean reads exist — a floor parked inside the 12288..16384 dead band re-triggers on every pass (the exact "kept region lands over the trigger" loop class gh-1425 built the valve for)

**Empirical reproduction on this runner** (linux x64, this repo's own CI toolchain — flutter 3.47.7 / Dart 3.13.5, where openpty works, unlike the author's host):

```
dart test --tags integration test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart
→ 0 tests passed, 1 failed
→ header_badge_pty_test.dart:98 — the E1 `hi!` wait, TimeoutException after 90 s
→ captured status row: «ctx 80% (13.0k/16.4k) · 0tok · turn 3» with
  «Compacting context…» live mid-E1, composer still holding `say hi`
```

That is the **same mid-compaction-at-timeout face as the Oct-14 nightly red** (job 38506597725), now on the fixed code. Everything through turn 1 passes (fold receipt, badge, `done: recovered`, badge-clear) — only the leg this PR claims to have made impossible is still broken. Note the E1 compaction also re-risks the E1 assertion at `header_badge_pty_test.dart:104-107`: a pre-flight fold prints its own `● auto-compacted` receipt — the badge-free-fresh-run contract this test exists to pin.

**Fix direction** — the floor is dominated by the fixed 8-record protected tail plus ~5.5k overhead, so *count* changes alone can't lower it; shrink the per-read size and grow the count so both lines clear with real margin, e.g. **30 × 60-line reads**: turn-1 second request ≈ 30 × 615 ≈ 18.5k > 16384 (guard/fold premise intact, ~2.1k margin) while the E1 floor drops to ≈ 8 × 615 + 5.5k ≈ **10.4k < 12288 (~1.9k margin under the actual trigger)**. Re-derive from `CompactionSettings.forWindow(window)` arithmetic, re-measure, and please include the PTY leg this time (it runs fine on linux hosted runners).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: pin the scenario shape to the production constants it leans on**

The whole fix is arithmetic over production constants — `hideProtectTailEntries = 8` (`lib/src/compaction/structured/judge.dart:16`), `chars / 4` estimation (`lib/src/compaction/token_estimation.dart:32`), and the `shouldCompact` trigger (`window − window~/4`, `compaction.dart:452,488`) — but nothing static guards that coupling: this file is quarantined (`scripts/test_quarantine.json`, nightly-only) and the compactor unit tests know nothing of this scenario. If any constant moves (tail protection grows, estimator changes, cap knob semantics shift), the floor silently re-crosses a line and the nightly goes red again with zero gate-time signal.

A cheap guard in the test body turns that into an immediate failure with the arithmetic spelled out:

```dart
import 'package:flutter_agent_harness/src/compaction/structured/judge.dart'
    show hideProtectTailEntries;

// The post-fold E1 floor is the protected tail plus fixed overhead; it
// must stay under the shouldCompact trigger (window − window ~/ 4), not
// just under the guard line — see the scenario comment above.
const window = 16384;
const perReadTokens = (90 * 41 / 4).ceil(); // 40-char lines + newline, /4
final e1Floor = hideProtectTailEntries * perReadTokens + 5500;
expect(
  e1Floor,
  lessThan((window - window ~/ 4) - 1500),
  reason: 'lean-read scenario assumes the E1 floor clears the '
      'shouldCompact trigger with margin',
);
```

(Other tests already import package internals — e.g. `test/compaction/structured_ledger_test.dart` imports `judge.dart` directly — so the coupling costs nothing stylistically. Keep the constants symbolic so a rework of the loop bounds updates the guard in the same edit.)

---

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-14):

Fixed in 4de34b852f — took your exact direction. Scenario is now 30 x 60-line reads: turn-1 second request = 30 x 615 = 18450 > 16384 (fold premise intact), E1 floor = 8 x 615 + 5.5k = 10420 < 12288 (~1.9k margin under the shouldCompact trigger). Your arithmetic, your numbers. Verified headlessly on the full CLI stack: turn-1 guard fires -> structured relief + classic fall-through -> done: recovered, then E1 answers hi! with the transcript floor measured at ~610 tokens (production basis = floor + your 5.5k overhead, comfortably under the trigger; my harness wiring carries a LARGER overhead than the test config since it cannot restrict tools, so it is a conservative upper bound). The E1-badge-free risk you flagged is also gone: with the floor under the trigger the pre-flight never runs at E1, so no second receipt can print in the fresh run. Re the PTY leg: agreed it runs on linux hosted runners — I cannot execute it on this host (no openpty, environmental, disclosed in the PR body); your CI reproduction of the previous head is itself the runner-class evidence, and the re-run on this head is the proof for the fix.

- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain

- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T06:51:31Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1597
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1597
- **Title**: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/header-badge-pty-nightly` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +64
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T04:58:26Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T06:51:31Z

## PR Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598"

|---|---|---|---|---|

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598

# pr-1597: fix: nightly header_badge_pty red 4 nights — the badge scenario rode the overflow razor edge; E1 flipped into the relief chain

## Description

## Evidence — nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (nightly red, no issue)

| run | night | head sha | failing line | face |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 38109027033 | Oct-11 | e294e0434c | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print fused into the glass |
| 38200898584 | Oct-12 | bfb65bd117 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38342692870 | Oct-13 | 0459018236 | L61 (badge, 30s) | SUMMARIZE print |
| 38506597725 | Oct-14 | 869c4666ef | **L86 (E1 `hi!`, 90s)** | **new face: mid-relief at timeout** |

Last green nightly: 38021029680 (Oct-10, d19cf5be98). PR-path CI is green everywhere — the suite is nightly-only.

## Root cause — two stacked faces

**Face 1 (Oct-11/12/13): the structured compactor carried a leftover `SUMMARIZE n=…` debug `print` (landed with #1453, Oct-10)** that wrote raw bytes into the live TUI glass mid-run, desyncing the cell-diff painter; the status-row fold badge painted, was clobbered, and the badge wait timed out with the turn already settled. **Already root-caused and removed on main by #1495 (Oct-13)** — captured screens show `SUMMARIZE n=9 :: assistant:Instance of…` fused between fold rules (jobs 114115713413, 114137491055, 114167806111). This PR carries that fix forward (it is on main).

**Face 2 (Oct-14, the residue): the scenario itself rides the overflow razor edge.** The fold's post-compaction floor is the protected live-edge tail (the last 8 ledger records, `hideProtectTailEntries = 8`): with 8 fat reads, that floor ≈ the whole transcript, so the E1 `say hi` request sits within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line — exactly as #1495 documented («its post-fold context rides within ~1k tokens of the gross-overflow line, so host estimator jitter flips it into another relief chain»). When E1 flips over:

- the over-window guard fires and the relief chain runs — it is **healthy** (verified headlessly end-to-end: guard → structured passes → classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → retried → reply) but **wall-clock-bounded by design** (judge attempt budget 300s, structured total 15min, issue #541);
- a loaded nightly runner (the same box was also going red on `subagent_integration_test` on Oct-11/12) can legally hold the turn past any fixed 90s wait;
- the Oct-14 capture matches mid-relief exactly: status meter still repainting (`5` cells mid-update in the raw tail), paused notice on the glass, `0tok`, **no** `[resuming]` note, **no** error row — the chain never finished inside 90s.

The judge pick structure makes it worse: the mock judge's `[2]` snaps to the reads-turn pair group, which touches the protected tail and is dropped entirely (`records: 0 hidden` in every captured receipt) — the relief structurally cannot free the tail, so a flipped E1 can only grind through consolidation crumbs.

n.b. the 4/4 deterministic shas conflate the two faces: the print explains 3 of 4 (fixed Oct-13); the E1 face has a sample size of **one** (the only night that ran post-print-fix code) and is jitter/timing-dependent by mechanism — flake-class for that leg, fixed here by removing the dependence instead of quarantining.

## Fix — the scenario, not the assertions

`test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` only:

- **8 fat reads (300 lines) → 24 lean reads (90 lines).** Same overflow at turn-1's second request (~22k tool-result tokens vs the 16384 cap → guard → fold → badge — the scenario's premise is unchanged), but the protected-tail floor drops out: the E1 request lands at **~12.9k tokens against the 16384 guard line (~3.4k headroom, measured)**, so E1 can never enter relief at all — the flip the whole residue hung on becomes impossible.
- Comments updated to the real arithmetic; **every assertion and both 90s budgets untouched** (the budgets stay as loaded-runner headroom, per #1495's intent).

## Verification

- `dart analyze test/integration/header_badge_pty_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full headless reproduction of the exact scenario (real CLI stack, scripted SSE-equivalent stream, production-shaped overhead): turn-1 guard fires → structured passes + classic fall-through → `[resuming]` → `done: recovered` → E1 answers `hi!` with request basis **12898 tokens** — 3.4k under the guard line. Relief chain completes in ~0.2s against instant mocks; E1 never enters it.
- **Honest disclosure: the PTY leg cannot run on this host** (no openpty — environmental; two prior lanes hit the same wall). The nightly run on this PR branch (or the next nightly after merge) is the final proof; the headless drive plus the captured-screen forensics above are the local evidence.

Fixes nothing — reference: nightly red 2026-10-11..14 (supersedes the quarantine commit 1888f7ccbe's premise: the test is not a flake, its scenario was razor-edged).

Closes #1598
